Controllability and stabilizability analysis

Source: R/controllability.R
ctrl_controllability.Rd

Determine the controllable subspace with an orthogonal staircase reduction, which is far better conditioned than the rank of the controllability matrix. The uncontrollable modes are the eigenvalues of the uncontrollable block. The model is stabilizable when every uncontrollable mode is asymptotically stable; full controllability is not required.

Usage

ctrl_controllability(sys, B = NULL, tol = NULL, discrete = NULL)

Arguments

sys

A ctrl_ss model (or the matrix A).

B

Input matrix when sys is a matrix.

tol

Rank tolerance.

discrete

Time domain when sys is a matrix (FALSE by default).

Value

A list of class ctrl_controllability with rank, n, controllable, stabilizable, uncontrollable_modes, basis (an orthonormal basis of the controllable subspace), transform (the orthogonal staircase transformation), pbh (table of PBH tests) and ctrb_singular_values.

Details

Rank decisions use the tolerance tol, scaled by the norms of A and B. A rank computed under a tolerance is a numerical statement: a nearly uncontrollable system can be reported as controllable with a tiny PBH singular value. Inspect pbh$pbh_sigma_min (the smallest singular value of \([A - \lambda I, B]\) for each eigenvalue) to judge the distance to uncontrollability.

Examples

A <- diag(c(-1, 2))
B <- c(1, 0)
res <- ctrl_controllability(A, B)
res$controllable
#> [1] FALSE
res$stabilizable  # the unstable mode at 2 is uncontrollable
#> [1] FALSE
